usb-ports.gadgetZero.note: A device's name (USB menu, Machines page's USB tab, messages about attaching): the controller's built-in test device, attached with ?usbzero=1.

usb-ports.builtinKeyboard.note: A device's name (USB menu, messages about attaching): the machine's own USB boot keyboard on the last connector, which carries the screen's keys to the firmware.

usb-ports.testDevice.note: A device's name for a virtual test device of another kind, where a sentence names the device ("… couldn't be attached"); lowercase, as it may stand mid-sentence.

usb-ports.usbDevice.note: A WebUSB device's name when it gives no product name (USB menu, Machines page's USB tab, messages). {{ids}} is its vendor and product IDs as lsusb prints them, e.g. 2e8a:000a.

usb-ports.hidDevice.note: A WebHID device's name when it gives no product name (USB menu, Machines page's USB tab, messages). {{ids}} is its vendor and product IDs as lsusb prints them, e.g. 054c:0ce6.

usb-ports.class.audio.note: A USB interface class's name (audio), lowercase, placed in the problem "Interface N is a {{class}} interface, which the browser keeps from pages…" (USB menu, Machines page's USB tab).

usb-ports.class.cdc.note: A USB interface class's name (communications (CDC)), lowercase, placed in the problem "Interface N is a {{class}} interface, which the browser keeps from pages…" (USB menu, Machines page's USB tab).

usb-ports.class.hid.note: A USB interface class's name (HID), lowercase, placed in the problem "Interface N is a {{class}} interface, which the browser keeps from pages…" (USB menu, Machines page's USB tab).

usb-ports.class.stillImage.note: A USB interface class's name (still image), lowercase, placed in the problem "Interface N is a {{class}} interface, which the browser keeps from pages…" (USB menu, Machines page's USB tab).

usb-ports.class.printer.note: A USB interface class's name (printer), lowercase, placed in the problem "Interface N is a {{class}} interface, which the browser keeps from pages…" (USB menu, Machines page's USB tab).

usb-ports.class.massStorage.note: A USB interface class's name (mass storage), lowercase, placed in the problem "Interface N is a {{class}} interface, which the browser keeps from pages…" (USB menu, Machines page's USB tab).

usb-ports.class.hub.note: A USB interface class's name (hub), lowercase, placed in the problem "Interface N is a {{class}} interface, which the browser keeps from pages…" (USB menu, Machines page's USB tab).

usb-ports.class.cdcData.note: A USB interface class's name (CDC data), lowercase, placed in the problem "Interface N is a {{class}} interface, which the browser keeps from pages…" (USB menu, Machines page's USB tab).

usb-ports.class.smartCard.note: A USB interface class's name (smart card), lowercase, placed in the problem "Interface N is a {{class}} interface, which the browser keeps from pages…" (USB menu, Machines page's USB tab).

usb-ports.class.video.note: A USB interface class's name (video), lowercase, placed in the problem "Interface N is a {{class}} interface, which the browser keeps from pages…" (USB menu, Machines page's USB tab).

usb-ports.class.audioVideo.note: A USB interface class's name (audio/video), lowercase, placed in the problem "Interface N is a {{class}} interface, which the browser keeps from pages…" (USB menu, Machines page's USB tab).

usb-ports.class.bluetooth.note: A USB interface class's name (wireless controller (Bluetooth)), lowercase, placed in the problem "Interface N is a {{class}} interface, which the browser keeps from pages…" (USB menu, Machines page's USB tab).

usb-ports.class.dfu.note: A USB interface class's name (DFU), lowercase, placed in the problem "Interface N is a {{class}} interface, which the browser keeps from pages…" (USB menu, Machines page's USB tab).

usb-ports.class.vendor.note: A USB interface class's name (vendor-specific), lowercase, placed in the problem "Interface N is a {{class}} interface, which the browser keeps from pages…" (USB menu, Machines page's USB tab).

usb-ports.class.other.note: A USB interface class without a name of its own, placed in the problem "Interface N is a {{class}} interface…". {{code}} is the class number in hex, e.g. 0x0f.

usb-ports.usage.pointer.note: A HID collection's kind (pointer), lowercase, placed in the problem "The device's {{what}} part is kept from pages by the browser…" about a HID device (USB menu, Machines page's USB tab).

usb-ports.usage.mouse.note: A HID collection's kind (mouse), lowercase, placed in the problem "The device's {{what}} part is kept from pages by the browser…" about a HID device (USB menu, Machines page's USB tab).

usb-ports.usage.keyboard.note: A HID collection's kind (keyboard), lowercase, placed in the problem "The device's {{what}} part is kept from pages by the browser…" about a HID device (USB menu, Machines page's USB tab).

usb-ports.usage.keypad.note: A HID collection's kind (keypad), lowercase, placed in the problem "The device's {{what}} part is kept from pages by the browser…" about a HID device (USB menu, Machines page's USB tab).

usb-ports.usage.systemControl.note: A HID collection's kind (system control), lowercase, placed in the problem "The device's {{what}} part is kept from pages by the browser…" about a HID device (USB menu, Machines page's USB tab).

usb-ports.usage.other.note: A HID collection without a name of its own, placed in the problem "The device's {{what}} part is kept from pages…". {{usage}} is its usage page and usage in hex, e.g. 000c:0001.

usb-ports.protectedInterface.hid.message: Interface {{interface}} is a {{class}} interface, which the browser keeps from pages: the guest doesn't see it. Its HID part can come in as a HID device instead (Add a device…, then a HID device), unless it is a keyboard or a mouse: the machine has the page's.
usb-ports.protectedInterface.hid.note: A problem under a WebUSB device attached with part of it left out (Machines page's USB tab, the USB menu's tooltip, an attach's error). {{interface}} is the interface number; {{class}} its class's name (usb-ports.class.*). This variant is for a HID interface: it says where to go instead.

usb-ports.protectedInterface.disk.message: Interface {{interface}} is a {{class}} interface, which the browser keeps from pages: the guest doesn't see it. A disk image comes in through the machine's Disks instead.
usb-ports.protectedInterface.disk.note: A problem under a WebUSB device attached with part of it left out (Machines page's USB tab, the USB menu's tooltip, an attach's error). {{interface}} is the interface number; {{class}} its class's name (usb-ports.class.*). This variant is for a mass storage interface.

usb-ports.protectedInterface.sound.message: Interface {{interface}} is a {{class}} interface, which the browser keeps from pages: the guest doesn't see it. Sound goes through the machine's sound card (and the microphone), which the page has.
usb-ports.protectedInterface.sound.note: A problem under a WebUSB device attached with part of it left out (Machines page's USB tab, the USB menu's tooltip, an attach's error). {{interface}} is the interface number; {{class}} its class's name (usb-ports.class.*). This variant is for an audio or video interface.

usb-ports.protectedInterface.bluetooth.message: Interface {{interface}} is a {{class}} interface, which the browser keeps from pages: the guest doesn't see it. A browser has no way to a Bluetooth adapter.
usb-ports.protectedInterface.bluetooth.note: A problem under a WebUSB device attached with part of it left out (Machines page's USB tab, the USB menu's tooltip, an attach's error). {{interface}} is the interface number; {{class}} its class's name (usb-ports.class.*). This variant is for a Bluetooth adapter.

usb-ports.protectedInterface.message: Interface {{interface}} is a {{class}} interface, which the browser keeps from pages: the guest doesn't see it.
usb-ports.protectedInterface.note: A problem under a WebUSB device attached with part of it left out (Machines page's USB tab, the USB menu's tooltip, an attach's error). {{interface}} is the interface number; {{class}} its class's name (usb-ports.class.*). This variant is for any other class (no route elsewhere).

usb-ports.browserSaid.note: Line under a USB problem's folded details (Machines page's USB tab, Add a USB device, the USB menu's error): the browser's own error message. {{said}} is that message, in the browser's words.

usb-ports.zadig.message: Install the WinUSB driver for it with Zadig: Options, List All Devices, pick the device, WinUSB, Replace Driver.
usb-ports.zadig.note: Step 1 of the Windows remedy under a USB problem (folded, with a link to zadig.akeo.ie): how to give the device the driver a browser needs. Zadig's menu items are named as Zadig names them.

usb-ports.zadig.interface.message: Install the WinUSB driver for it with Zadig: Options, List All Devices, pick the device's interface {{interface}}, WinUSB, Replace Driver.
usb-ports.zadig.interface.note: Step 1 of the Windows remedy for an interface something else holds (folded under the problem, with a link to zadig.akeo.ie). {{interface}} is the interface number.

usb-ports.replug.message: Unplug the device, plug it in again, then attach it.
usb-ports.replug.note: Last step of a USB remedy (Windows' driver, Linux's udev rule), numbered in the folded details under the problem.

usb-ports.claimFailed.message: Something on this computer is already using it (interface {{interface}}), so the browser can't pass it to the machine.
usb-ports.claimFailed.note: A USB problem's short text (Machines page's USB tab, USB menu, an attach's error): a driver or program on the host holds an interface; the OS's remedy is folded under it. {{interface}} is the interface number.

usb-ports.claimFailed.linux.message: How to free it on Linux
usb-ports.claimFailed.linux.note: Title of the folded remedy (a summary to click) under the problem "Something on this computer is already using it…", on a Linux host.

usb-ports.claimFailed.linux.driver.message: Find the kernel driver that holds it (such as cdc_acm, ftdi_sio, cp210x, ch341 or usblp):
usb-ports.claimFailed.linux.driver.note: Step 1 of the Linux remedy for an interface a driver holds; a command to copy (lsusb -t) follows. The driver names are Linux's.

usb-ports.claimFailed.linux.name.message: Find the interface's name under that driver (such as {{name}}):
usb-ports.claimFailed.linux.name.note: Step 2 of the Linux remedy for an interface a driver holds; a command to copy follows. {{name}} is an example of a sysfs interface name, e.g. 1-2:1.0.

usb-ports.claimFailed.linux.unbind.message: Unbind it; it stays free until the device is plugged in again:
usb-ports.claimFailed.linux.unbind.note: Step 3 of the Linux remedy for an interface a driver holds; the unbind command to copy follows.

usb-ports.claimFailed.linux.again.note: Step 4, the last, of the Linux remedy for an interface a driver holds.

usb-ports.claimFailed.linux.blacklist.message: To keep the driver off for good (for every device it serves), add this line to a file in /etc/modprobe.d/:
usb-ports.claimFailed.linux.blacklist.note: Note after the Linux remedy's steps for an interface a driver holds; the line to add (blacklist <driver>) follows.

usb-ports.claimFailed.mac.note: Title of the folded remedy under the problem "Something on this computer is already using it…", on a Mac.

usb-ports.claimFailed.mac.quit.message: Quit any app that uses the device, then attach it again.
usb-ports.claimFailed.mac.quit.note: The one step of the macOS remedy for an interface something holds.

usb-ports.claimFailed.mac.note.message: macOS's own drivers keep serial devices (CDC serial, serial adapters), and a page can't take them: if one of those holds it, the device can't reach the machine from this computer.
usb-ports.claimFailed.mac.note.note: Note after the macOS remedy's step for an interface something holds.

usb-ports.claimFailed.windows.message: How to free it on Windows
usb-ports.claimFailed.windows.note: Title of the folded remedy under the problem "Something on this computer is already using it…", on Windows (Zadig's steps follow).

usb-ports.claimFailed.windows.note.message: Windows' own programs then no longer see that interface.
usb-ports.claimFailed.windows.note.note: Note after the Windows remedy's steps (the WinUSB driver through Zadig) for an interface something holds.

usb-ports.claimFailed.other.message: Something on this computer is already using it (interface {{interface}}), so the browser can't pass it to the machine. Close what uses it on this computer, then attach it again.
usb-ports.claimFailed.other.note: A USB problem's text on a host without a remedy of its own (ChromeOS, other): a driver or program holds an interface. {{interface}} is the interface number.

usb-ports.protectedCollection.kept.message: The device's {{what}} part is kept from pages by the browser, all but its feature reports (its settings, which tools such as VIA use): the guest gets only those. The machine has the page's keyboard and mouse already.
usb-ports.protectedCollection.kept.note: A problem under an attached WebHID device (Machines page's USB tab, USB menu's tooltip): one of its collections reaches the guest only through its feature reports. {{what}} is the collection's kind (usb-ports.usage.*).

usb-ports.protectedCollection.message: The device's {{what}} part is kept from pages by the browser: the guest doesn't get it. The machine has the page's keyboard and mouse already.
usb-ports.protectedCollection.note: A problem under an attached WebHID device (Machines page's USB tab, USB menu's tooltip): one of its collections doesn't reach the guest. {{what}} is the collection's kind (usb-ports.usage.*).

usb-ports.noCollections.message: Everything this HID device offers is kept from pages by the browser (a keyboard's keys, a mouse's pointer, a security key): nothing is left for the guest. The machine has the page's keyboard and mouse already.
usb-ports.noCollections.note: A problem under a WebHID device that couldn't be attached (an attach's error in the USB menu, Add a USB device, the Machines page): nothing of it reaches pages.

usb-ports.openFailed.linux.message: The browser couldn't open it: your user probably has no permission to use it.
usb-ports.openFailed.linux.note: A problem when a USB or HID device couldn't be opened, on a Linux host (an attach's error); the udev remedy is folded under it, with the browser's own message.

usb-ports.openFailed.linux.title.message: How to give your user access on Linux
usb-ports.openFailed.linux.title.note: Title of the folded remedy (a udev rule) under the problem "The browser couldn't open it: your user probably has no permission…".

usb-ports.openFailed.linux.udev.note: Step 1 of the Linux remedy for a device the user may not open; the rule to copy follows.

usb-ports.openFailed.linux.reload.note: Step 2 of the Linux remedy for a device the user may not open; the command to copy follows.

usb-ports.openFailed.windows.message: The browser couldn't open it: on Windows it needs the WinUSB driver.
usb-ports.openFailed.windows.note: A problem when a WebUSB device couldn't be opened on Windows (an attach's error); Zadig's steps are folded under it.

usb-ports.openFailed.windows.title.note: Title of the folded remedy (installing WinUSB with Zadig) under the problem "The browser couldn't open it: on Windows it needs the WinUSB driver."

usb-ports.openFailed.other.message: The browser couldn't open it: another program may have it open. Close that program, then attach the device again.
usb-ports.openFailed.other.note: A problem when a device couldn't be opened, on a host without a remedy of its own (an attach's error); the browser's own message is folded under it.

usb-live.noWebUsb.message: This browser has no WebUSB (Chromium and Chrome do).
usb-live.noWebUsb.note: Error (message bar, Add a USB device) when a USB device is to be picked in a browser without WebUSB.

usb-live.noWebHid.message: This browser has no WebHID (Chromium and Chrome do).
usb-live.noWebHid.note: Error (message bar, Add a USB device) when a HID device is to be picked in a browser without WebHID.

usb-live.notAttached.note: Headline of an attach's error when the device worker said why (USB menu, Add a USB device, Machines page's USB tab, message bar): the problems and their remedies follow under it. {{name}} is the device's name.

usb-live.noAnswer.message: The machine's USB controller didn't answer: is it still running?
usb-live.noAnswer.note: Error when an attach or a detach got no answer from the running machine in time (USB menu, Machines page's USB tab, message bar).

usb-live.connectorTaken.note: Error when a device is attached on a connector another device is on (USB menu, Machines page's USB tab). {{connector}} is the connector's number (from 1); {{name}} the device on it.

usb-live.connectorInUse.note: Error when another device took the connector while this one waited for its lock (USB menu, Machines page's USB tab). {{connector}} is the connector's number (from 1).

usb-live.stopped.note: Error of an attach or a detach still waiting when the machine stopped (USB menu, Machines page's USB tab, message bar).

usb.noWebUsb.note: Detail of an attach's error (message bar, USB menu): the machine's device worker has no WebUSB to open the device with. Lowercase: it follows a headline.

usb.noWebHid.note: Detail of an attach's error (message bar, USB menu): the machine's device worker has no WebHID to open the device with. Lowercase: it follows a headline.

usb.openFailed.note: Detail of an attach's error (message bar, USB menu) when the device worker couldn't open the device; why follows on the next line. Lowercase: it follows a headline.

usb.wentAway.message: the machine went away while it opened
usb.wentAway.note: Detail of an attach's error (message bar, USB menu): the machine stopped while the device was being opened. Lowercase: it follows a headline.

webusb.openFailed.note: Detail of an attach's error (message bar, USB menu) when the browser refused to open a USB or HID device; the browser's own words follow on the next line. Lowercase: it follows a headline.

webusb.readFailed.note: Detail of an attach's error (message bar, USB menu) when a WebUSB device's descriptors couldn't be read; the browser's own words follow on the next line. Lowercase: it follows a headline.

webusb.noInterface.message: no interface of the device can be used through WebUSB
webusb.noInterface.note: Detail of an attach's error (message bar, USB menu) when every interface of a WebUSB device is kept from pages or held; the problems follow. Lowercase: it follows a headline.

webusb.notFound.message: the device is not plugged in, or this page has no permission for it
webusb.notFound.note: Detail of an attach's error (message bar, USB menu) when the remembered device isn't among those the browser lists now. Lowercase: it follows a headline.

webhid.noCollections.message: WebHID shows none of this device's collections
webhid.noCollections.note: Detail of an attach's error (message bar, USB menu) when the browser hides all of a HID device. Lowercase: it follows a headline.

Usb.state.attached.note: A remembered USB device's state, at the end of its line on the Machines page's USB tab (lowercase, after ' · '): attached to the machine on this page.

Usb.state.plugged.note: A remembered USB device's state, at the end of its line on the Machines page's USB tab (lowercase, after ' · '): plugged into this computer, with permission, and attached nowhere.

Usb.state.unplugged.note: A remembered USB device's state, at the end of its line on the Machines page's USB tab (lowercase, after ' · '): granted but not plugged in now.

Usb.state.held.note: A remembered USB device's state, at the end of its line on the Machines page's USB tab (lowercase, after ' · '): attached to a machine in another tab that didn't say its name.

Usb.state.ungranted.note: A remembered USB device's state, at the end of its line on the Machines page's USB tab (lowercase, after ' · '): remembered, but this browser hasn't granted it (the machine came from another browser).

Usb.state.heldBy.note: A remembered USB device's state on the Machines page's USB tab: attached to another machine, in another tab. {{holder}} is that machine's name.

Usb.forget.attached.message: Forget {{name}}? It is detached first (the guest sees it unplugged). When no other machine remembers it, the browser's permission for it goes too.
Usb.forget.attached.note: Question (confirm dialog) on the Machines page's USB tab when Forget is clicked on a device attached to the running machine. {{name}} is the device's name.

Usb.forget.message: Forget {{name}}? When no other machine remembers it, the browser's permission for it goes too.
Usb.forget.note: Question (confirm dialog) on the Machines page's USB tab when Forget is clicked on a device not attached here. {{name}} is the device's name.

Usb.forget.title.note: Title of the confirm dialog that asks before a remembered USB device is forgotten (Machines page, USB tab).

Usb.forget.ok.note: OK button of the confirm dialog that asks before a remembered USB device is forgotten.

Usb.busy.forgetting.note: What the Machines page is doing (shown with … at its top) while a USB device is forgotten.

Usb.noController.message: This machine has no USB controller: turn it on above to attach devices. It changes the machine's shape, so the snapshots taken before are orphaned.
Usb.noController.note: Note at the top of the Machines page's USB tab for a machine whose USB controller is off (the switch is above it).

Usb.meta.usb.note: The start of a remembered WebUSB device's details line (Machines page, USB tab, under its name). {{ids}} is its vendor and product IDs, e.g. 2e8a:000a.

Usb.meta.hid.note: The start of a remembered WebHID device's details line (Machines page, USB tab, under its name). {{ids}} is its vendor and product IDs, e.g. 054c:0ce6.

Usb.meta.serial.note: Part of a remembered USB device's details line (Machines page, USB tab), after ' · ': its serial number, {{serial}}.

Usb.meta.index.nd.note: Part of a remembered USB device's details line (Machines page, USB tab), after ' · ', for the second of identical devices without a serial number ({{n}} is 2): English's ordinal suffix is in the words, so the page picks nd, rd or th.

Usb.meta.index.rd.note: Part of a remembered USB device's details line (Machines page, USB tab), after ' · ', for the third of identical devices without a serial number ({{n}} is 3).

Usb.meta.index.th.note: Part of a remembered USB device's details line (Machines page, USB tab), after ' · ', for the fourth or later of identical devices without a serial number ({{n}} is its place, 4 and up).

Usb.connector.title.message: The root connector it goes on (the guest's port path: its names under /dev/serial/by-path stay the same)
Usb.connector.title.note: Tooltip of a remembered USB device's Connector field (Machines page, USB tab).

Usb.connector.note: Label of a remembered USB device's connector choice (1–4), on its line on the Machines page's USB tab.

Usb.busy.saving.note: What the Machines page is doing (shown with … at its top) while a USB device's connector or At start is saved.

Usb.atStart.title.message: Attached when the machine starts, and when it is plugged in while the machine runs
Usb.atStart.title.note: Tooltip of a remembered USB device's At start checkbox (Machines page, USB tab).

Usb.atStart.note: Checkbox on a remembered USB device's line (Machines page, USB tab): the device is attached when the machine starts.

Usb.busy.asking.note: What the Machines page is doing (shown with … at its top) while the browser's chooser asks for a USB device's permission.

Usb.allow.title.message: The browser's chooser, showing this device: pick it to give this page its permission
Usb.allow.title.note: Tooltip of a USB device's Allow… button (Machines page, USB tab).

Usb.allow.note: Button on a remembered USB device this browser has no permission for (Machines page, USB tab): opens the browser's chooser.

Usb.busy.detaching.note: What the Machines page is doing (shown with … at its top) while a USB device is detached.

Usb.detach.title.note: Tooltip of an attached USB device's Detach button (Machines page, USB tab).

Usb.detach.note: Button on a USB device attached to the machine running on this page (Machines page, USB tab): unplugs it from the guest.

Usb.busy.attaching.note: What the Machines page is doing (shown with … at its top) while a USB device is attached.

Usb.attachHere.title.message: Another machine has it: it is detached there first (asked)
Usb.attachHere.title.note: Tooltip of the Attach here… button on a USB device another machine holds (Machines page, USB tab).

Usb.attach.title.note: Tooltip of a plugged-in USB device's Attach button (Machines page, USB tab).

Usb.attachHere.note: Button on a USB device another machine holds, while this machine runs on the page (Machines page, USB tab): asks, then takes it.

Usb.attach.note: Button on a plugged-in USB device while the machine runs on this page (Machines page, USB tab): plugs it into the guest.

Usb.forget.button.title.message: The machine no longer remembers it
Usb.forget.button.title.note: Tooltip of a remembered USB device's Forget button (Machines page, USB tab).

Usb.forget.button.note: Button on each remembered USB device (Machines page, USB tab): the machine forgets it (asked first).

Usb.none.note: The Machines page's USB tab's list when the machine remembers no device.

Usb.builtin.pluggedNow.message: Connector {{connector}} is the built-in keyboard's: the screen's keys reach the firmware and the boot loader through it, until the guest's own keyboard driver takes over (then it is unplugged, now it is plugged in).
Usb.builtin.pluggedNow.note: Note on the Machines page's USB tab, for the machine running on this page while its built-in keyboard is plugged in. {{connector}} is the keyboard's connector number (from 1).

Usb.builtin.asNow.message: Connector {{connector}} is the built-in keyboard's: the screen's keys reach the firmware and the boot loader through it, until the guest's own keyboard driver takes over (then it is unplugged, as now).
Usb.builtin.asNow.note: Note on the Machines page's USB tab, for the machine running on this page while its built-in keyboard is unplugged (the guest's driver took over). {{connector}} is the keyboard's connector number (from 1).

Usb.builtin.message: Connector {{connector}} is the built-in keyboard's: the screen's keys reach the firmware and the boot loader through it, until the guest's own keyboard driver takes over (then it is unplugged).
Usb.builtin.note: Note on the Machines page's USB tab, for a machine that isn't running on this page. {{connector}} is the built-in keyboard's connector number (from 1).

Usb.add.note: Button under the remembered devices (Machines page, USB tab): opens the Add a USB device wizard.

Usb.twins.message: Identical devices without a serial number are told apart by the order the browser lists them in (usually the order they were plugged in): plug them in the same order, or the guest sees them swapped.
Usb.twins.note: Note on the Machines page's USB tab, shown when the machine remembers identical devices without a serial number.

Usb.note.otherTab.message: It runs in another tab: attach and detach there. Devices aren't part of the machine's shape: they are plugged in and out while it runs, and Snapshot and Suspend unplug them first (asked).
Usb.note.otherTab.note: Note at the bottom of the Machines page's USB tab while the machine runs in another tab.

Usb.note.stopped.message: Attach and detach while the machine runs on this page (its toolbar has a USB menu). Devices aren't part of the machine's shape: they are plugged in and out while it runs, and Snapshot and Suspend unplug them first (asked).
Usb.note.stopped.note: Note at the bottom of the Machines page's USB tab while the machine isn't running.

Usb.note.message: Devices aren't part of the machine's shape: they are plugged in and out while it runs, and Snapshot and Suspend unplug them first (asked).
Usb.note.note: Note at the bottom of the Machines page's USB tab while the machine runs on this page.

UsbMenu.why.unplugged.note: Tooltip of a remembered device's line in the toolbar's USB menu when it isn't plugged in (its checkbox is off).

UsbMenu.why.heldBy.note: Tooltip of a remembered device's line in the USB menu when another machine, in another tab, has it. {{holder}} is that machine's name.

UsbMenu.why.held.note: Tooltip of a remembered device's line in the USB menu when another machine, in another tab that didn't say its name, has it.

UsbMenu.why.ungranted.message: No permission in this browser yet: Allow it on the Machines page's USB tab
UsbMenu.why.ungranted.note: Tooltip of a remembered device's line in the USB menu when this browser hasn't granted it (its checkbox is off).

UsbMenu.where.detaching.note: Right side of a device's line in the toolbar's USB menu while it is being detached.

UsbMenu.where.attaching.note: Right side of a device's line in the toolbar's USB menu while it is being attached.

UsbMenu.where.connector.note: Right side of an attached device's line in the toolbar's USB menu: the connector it is on. {{connector}} is its number (from 1).

UsbMenu.where.heldBy.note: Right side of a device's line in the toolbar's USB menu when another machine has it. {{holder}} is that machine's name.

UsbMenu.where.held.note: Right side of a device's line in the toolbar's USB menu when another machine (that didn't say its name) has it.

UsbMenu.where.ungranted.note: Right side of a device's line in the toolbar's USB menu when this browser hasn't granted it.

UsbMenu.where.unplugged.note: Right side of a device's line in the toolbar's USB menu when it isn't plugged in.

UsbMenu.title.message: USB devices: attach them to the machine, or add one
UsbMenu.title.note: Tooltip of the toolbar's USB menu button.

UsbMenu.attached.note: Screen-reader name of the count badge on the toolbar's USB button. {{n}} is the number of devices attached (1 or more).

UsbMenu.notNow.note: Button of an offer at the top of the USB menu (a device plugged in, one unplugged, a permission to give): dismisses the offer.

UsbMenu.problems.message: Part of it doesn't reach the guest: hover here, or see All USB settings…
UsbMenu.problems.note: Warning under an attached device in the toolbar's USB menu when part of it is kept from the guest; its tooltip lists what.

UsbMenu.none.note: The toolbar's USB menu's list when the machine remembers no device.

UsbMenu.zero.note: Name of the controller's test device in the USB menu (with ?usbzero=1), beside its checkbox.

UsbMenu.zero.note.note: What Gadget Zero is, at the right of its line in the USB menu (with ?usbzero=1).

UsbMenu.add.note: Button in the toolbar's USB menu: opens the Add a USB device wizard.

UsbMenu.all.note: Button in the toolbar's USB menu: opens the Machines page's USB tab for this machine.

UsbMenu.stopped.message: The machine isn't running: its devices are attached when it runs.
UsbMenu.stopped.note: Hint at the bottom of the toolbar's USB menu while the machine isn't running.

AddUsb.usb.note: Title of the first choice in the Add a USB device wizard: a device passed through over WebUSB.

AddUsb.usb.text.message: Developer and maker hardware, passed through as it is: microcontroller boards and debug probes, Android phones (adb, fastboot), USB-serial adapters, logic analysers, SDRs, printers. Not what the browser keeps from pages (keyboards, mice, disks, webcams, headsets, Bluetooth adapters), nor an interface a driver on this computer holds: the page says which and what to do.
AddUsb.usb.text.note: Explanation under A USB device (WebUSB), the first choice in the Add a USB device wizard.

AddUsb.hid.note: Title of the second choice in the Add a USB device wizard: a device built from what WebHID tells.

AddUsb.hid.text.message: Game pads, joysticks and wheels, macro pads and Stream Decks, a keyboard's configuration interface (VIA), a UPS. The guest gets a USB HID device built from what the browser tells of it, over USB or Bluetooth. A keyboard's keys and a mouse's pointer stay the browser's (the machine has the page's).
AddUsb.hid.text.note: Explanation under A HID device (WebHID), the second choice in the Add a USB device wizard.

AddUsb.title.note: Title of the Add a USB device wizard (a dialog from the USB menu or the Machines page's USB tab). {{name}} is the machine's name.

AddUsb.intro.message: Which kind? The browser then shows the devices it may give this page: pick one. The machine remembers it, and the browser keeps the permission.
AddUsb.intro.note: Text under the Add a USB device wizard's title, above the two kinds to choose from.

AddUsb.noWebUsb.note: Tooltip of the disabled WebUSB choice in the Add a USB device wizard, in a browser without WebUSB.

AddUsb.noWebHid.note: Tooltip of the disabled WebHID choice in the Add a USB device wizard, in a browser without WebHID.

AddUsb.cancel.note: Button that closes the Add a USB device wizard without adding anything.

UsbProblems.details.note: Title of the folded details (a summary to click) under a USB problem that has no remedy of its own, only the browser's message.
